title: Bug: BUFFER_PG profile configs are not applied correctly for lossless queues 3-4 after port breakout
author: AnandhiDhanabalan
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

For lossless queues, the BUFFER_PG profile is expected to be auto-generated by buffermgrd based on the port’s speed and cable length. This profile is applied to the lossless queues accordingly.

However, during port breakout, BUFFER_PG settings are applied only to the primary (first) port. The remaining breakout ports receive only the default configuration for lossless queues.

This behavior is due to buffermgrd relying on the port’s admin_status in CONFIG_DB to trigger BUFFER_PG application. Since the newly created breakout ports lack admin_status entries in CONFIG_DB, the configuration is deferred until the port’s admin_status is manually toggled to "up" or "down".

Adding admin_status entries for each port in /etc/sonic/port_breakout_config_db.json is cumbersome. 
A more streamlined approach is preferred to ensure consistent BUFFER_PG configuration for lossless queues across all breakout ports.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot up the device with the default profile, say 64x800G port profile.
2. Copy the breakout QoS/buffer configuration into /etc/sonic/port_breakout_config_db.json.
3. Break out a port (e.g., from 1x800G to 8x100G configuration).
4. Observe that the newly created breakout ports do not have the expected pg_lossless_100000_40m_profile applied.

**Example: Breakout Command and Resulting BUFFER_PG Entries**
**Apply Breakout Port**
`sudo config interface breakout Ethernet448 "8x100G[50G,25G]" -y -f -l
`

**Expected Profile on Breakout Port (First Port)**
```
admin@sonic:~$ redis-dump -d 4 -y -k "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet448|3-4"
{
  "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet448|3-4": {
    "expireat": 1747318206.0100954,
    "ttl": -0.001,
    "type": "hash",
    "value": {
      "profile": "pg_lossless_100000_40m_profile"
    }
  }
}
```

**Cable length and BUFFER_PG profile on other breakout ports**
```
admin@sonic:~$ redis-dump -d 4 -y -k "CABLE_LENGTH|AZURE" | grep Ethernet449
"Ethernet449": "40m"

admin@sonic:~$ redis-dump -d 4 -y -k "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet449|3-4"
{
  "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet449|3-4": {
    "expireat": 1747319244.7121916,
    "ttl": -0.001,
    "type": "hash",
    "value": {
      "profile": "ingress_lossless_profile"
    }
  }
}

admin@sonic:~$ redis-dump -d 4 -y -k "CABLE_LENGTH|AZURE" | grep Ethernet450
"Ethernet450": "40m"

admin@sonic:~$ redis-dump -d 4 -y -k "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet450|3-4"
{
  "BUFFER_PG|Ethernet450|3-4": {
    "expireat": 1747319278.028868,
    "ttl": -0.001,
    "type": "hash",
    "value": {
      "profile": "ingress_lossless_profile"
    }
  }
}
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual Behavior :** 
  Only the first break out port has pg_lossless_100000_40m_profile applied for BUFFER_PG for lossless queues.
  All other ports have default lossless profile applied.

**Expected Behavior:**
All the newly created breakout ports should have pg_lossless_100000_40m_profile applied for BUFFER_PG for lossless queues

linkedPullRequests.title: [buffermgrd]: Set admin_status down to ports with no admin_status
linkedPullRequests.author: rminnikanti
linkedPullRequests.body:
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/22931
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/23354 

**Why I did it:**
config_db producers like minigraph doesn't always set admin_status down for ports as admin_status default value is down.

This causes doSpeedUpdateTask() logic wait indefinitely for admin_status on ports.

During test execution, if sonic-mgmt test cases attempt to shut down interfaces that are not part of the topology, the "admin_status" for those interfaces is then added to CONFIG_DB. As a result, buffermgrd, which had been waiting for this field, immediately applies buffer profile updates to the interface. This unexpected behavior can lead to test case failures, particularly those involving checkpoint validations.

**How I did it**
Set admin_status down to ports with no admin_status

**How to verify it**
Run below testcase on T0 topology:
generic_config_updater/test_eth_interface.py::test_eth_interface_admin_change[down]

**Which release branch to backport (provide reason below if selected)**
* [ ]  202205
* [ ]  202211
* [ ]  202305
* [ ]  202311
* [ ]  202405
* [x]  202411
* [x]  202505

Tested branch (Please provide the tested image version)
 202411.0
 202505.0

**Description for the changelog**
[buffmgrd]: Set admin_status down to ports with no admin_status

Signed-off-by: Ravi Minnikanti <rminnikanti@marvell.com>
